title: 04. AsyncIO: AsyncIO Tasks and TaskGroups
summary: Covers Deep Dive into Tasks, TaskGroups (Python 3.11+), Cancellation Handling, Advanced Task Patterns, Task Scheduling Patterns.

sections.title: 9.1 Deep Dive into Tasks
sections.body:
### Visual Explanation

```
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                      TASK INTERNALS                                         ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣

║  │   │       return result                                          │  │   ║
║  │   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  │   + State tracking (pending/running/done/cancelled)                  │   ║
║  │   + Result storage                                                   │   ║
║  │   + Exception handling                                               │   ║

║  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   ║
║                                                                             ║
║  Key Methods:                                                               ║
║  ────────────                                                               ║
║  • task.result()      → Get result (raises if not done)                    ║
║  • task.exception()   → Get exception (if any)                             ║
║  • task.done()        → True if finished                                   ║
║  • task.cancelled()   → True if cancelled                                  ║
║  • task.cancel()      → Request cancellation                               ║
║  • task.add_done_callback(fn) → Call fn when done                          ║
║  • task.get_name()    → Get task name                                      ║
║                                                                             ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### Task States

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                           TASK STATES                                       │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│                     create_task()                                           │
│                          │                                                  │
│                          ▼                                                  │
│                    ┌───────────┐                                            │
│                    │  PENDING  │ ◄──────────────────────────────┐          │
│                    └─────┬─────┘                                 │          │
│                          │ Event loop schedules                  │          │
│                          ▼                                       │          │
│                    ┌───────────┐      await something      ┌─────┴─────┐   │
│                    │  RUNNING  │ ─────────────────────────►│ SUSPENDED │   │
│                    └─────┬─────┘                           └───────────┘   │
│                          │                                       │          │
│            ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐                        │          │
│            │             │             │                         │          │
│            ▼             ▼             ▼                         │          │
│     ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐ ┌───────────┐                   │          │
│     │ COMPLETED │ │  FAILED   │ │ CANCELLED │                   │          │
│     │ (result)  │ │(exception)│ │           │                   │          │
│     └───────────┘ └───────────┘ └───────────┘                   │          │
│                                                                             │
│  Note: Suspended → Pending when awaited thing completes                     │
│                                                                             │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: Task Properties and Methods

```python
import asyncio

async def sample_task(value, should_fail=False):
    """Sample task with optional failure"""
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    if should_fail:
        raise ValueError(f"Task failed with value {value}")
    return value * 2

async def main():
    # Create tasks
    task1 = asyncio.create_task(sample_task(21), name="Doubler")
    task2 = asyncio.create_task(sample_task(10, should_fail=True), name="Failer")

    # Check properties before completion
    print("=== Before Completion ===")
    print(f"task1.get_name(): {task1.get_name()}")
    print(f"task1.done(): {task1.done()}")
    print(f"task1.cancelled(): {task1.cancelled()}")

    # Wait for task1
    result = await task1
    print(f"\n=== After task1 Completion ===")
    print(f"task1.done(): {task1.done()}")
    print(f"task1.result(): {task1.result()}")

    # Handle task2 which will fail
    try:
        await task2
    except ValueError:
        pass

    print(f"\n=== After task2 Failure ===")
    print(f"task2.done(): {task2.done()}")
    print(f"task2.exception(): {task2.exception()}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 2: Task Callbacks

```python
import asyncio

def on_task_done(task):
    """Callback when task completes"""
    try:
        result = task.result()
        print(f"[Callback] Task {task.get_name()} completed with: {result}")
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print(f"[Callback] Task {task.get_name()} was cancelled")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[Callback] Task {task.get_name()} failed with: {e}")

async def worker(name, duration, fail=False):
    """Worker task"""
    await asyncio.sleep(duration)
    if fail:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} failed!")
    return f"{name} result"

async def main():
    # Create tasks with callbacks
    task1 = asyncio.create_task(worker("Task-A", 1), name="Task-A")
    task2 = asyncio.create_task(worker("Task-B", 0.5, fail=True), name="Task-B")
    task3 = asyncio.create_task(worker("Task-C", 2), name="Task-C")

    # Add callbacks
    task1.add_done_callback(on_task_done)
    task2.add_done_callback(on_task_done)
    task3.add_done_callback(on_task_done)

    # Wait a bit then cancel task3
    await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
    task3.cancel()

    # Wait for all to complete/cancel
    await asyncio.gather(task1, task2, task3, return_exceptions=True)

    print("\nAll tasks processed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

diagrams.title: Task states
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  p["Pending — scheduled"] --> r["Running"]
  r -->|await| s["Suspended"]
  s -->|"awaitable done"| r
  r -->|return| d["Done — result()"]
  r -->|raise| e["Done — exception()"]
  p -->|"cancel()"| x["Cancelled"]
  s -->|"cancel(): CancelledError at the await"| x
diagrams.explain: A Task wraps a coroutine and drives it on the loop. `done()` is True after a result, an exception or a cancellation. If a task fails and nobody retrieves the exception, asyncio logs "Task exception was never retrieved" when it is garbage-collected — a sign of fire-and-forget code.

sections.title: 9.2 TaskGroups (Python 3.11+)
sections.body:
### Visual Explanation

```
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                        TASKGROUP                                            ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                             ║
║  TaskGroup provides STRUCTURED CONCURRENCY:                                 ║
║                                                                             ║
║  async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:                                      ║
║      tg.create_task(coro1())                                                ║
║      tg.create_task(coro2())                                                ║
║      tg.create_task(coro3())                                                ║
║  # ALL tasks guaranteed to be done here                                     ║
║                                                                             ║
║  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  │   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │   ║
║  │   │                    TASKGROUP SCOPE                            │  │   ║
║  │   │                                                               │  │   ║
║  │   │    Task 1: ████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                │  │   ║
║  │   │    Task 2: ░░░░████████████████████░░░░░░░░░░                │  │   ║
║  │   │    Task 3: ░░░░░░░░████████████████████████████              │  │   ║
║  │   │                                              │               │  │   ║
║  │   │                                              ▼               │  │   ║
║  │   │                                    [All Complete]            │  │   ║
║  │   │                                                               │  │   ║
║  │   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │   ║
║  │   ▲                                              ▲                  │   ║
║  │   │ __aenter__                      __aexit__   │                  │   ║
║  │   │                                              │                  │   ║
║  │   └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘                  │   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   ║
║                                                                             ║
║  Key Guarantees:                                                            ║
║  ✅ All tasks complete before exiting the block                             ║
║  ✅ If any task fails, all others are cancelled                             ║
║  ✅ All exceptions are collected and raised as ExceptionGroup               ║
║  ✅ No orphan tasks possible                                                ║
║                                                                             ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### TaskGroup vs gather()

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TASKGROUP vs GATHER                                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│  asyncio.gather():                                                           │
│  • All tasks at once                                                         │
│  • First exception cancels others (default)                                  │
│  • No structured scope                                                       │
│  • return_exceptions=True for all exceptions                                 │
│                                                                              │
│  asyncio.TaskGroup():                                                        │
│  • Create tasks within scope                                                 │
│  • All exceptions collected as ExceptionGroup                                │
│  • Guaranteed cleanup                                                        │
│  • Better for dynamic task creation                                          │
│                                                                              │
│  Use TaskGroup when:                                                         │
│  • You need structured concurrency guarantees                                │
│  • Tasks are created dynamically                                             │
│  • You want all exceptions, not just first                                   │
│  • You need cancellation to propagate properly                               │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: Basic TaskGroup Usage

```python
import asyncio

async def fetch_data(name, delay):
    """Simulate fetching data"""
    print(f"[{name}] Starting...")
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    print(f"[{name}] Done!")
    return f"{name}_data"

async def main():
    results = []

    # TaskGroup ensures all tasks complete
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        task1 = tg.create_task(fetch_data("A", 1))
        task2 = tg.create_task(fetch_data("B", 0.5))
        task3 = tg.create_task(fetch_data("C", 1.5))

    # After the block, ALL tasks are done
    print("\nAll tasks completed!")
    print(f"Results: {task1.result()}, {task2.result()}, {task3.result()}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 2: TaskGroup Error Handling

```python
import asyncio

async def might_fail(name, fail=False):
    """Task that might fail"""
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    if fail:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} failed!")
    return f"{name} succeeded"

async def main():
    try:
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
            tg.create_task(might_fail("A", fail=False))
            tg.create_task(might_fail("B", fail=True))  # Will fail
            tg.create_task(might_fail("C", fail=True))  # Will also fail
            tg.create_task(might_fail("D", fail=False))
    except* ValueError as eg:
        # Python 3.11+ except* syntax for ExceptionGroup
        print(f"Caught {len(eg.exceptions)} ValueError(s):")
        for exc in eg.exceptions:
            print(f"  - {exc}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 3: Dynamic Task Creation in TaskGroup

```python
import asyncio
import random

async def process_item(item_id):
    """Process a single item"""
    duration = random.uniform(0.1, 0.5)
    await asyncio.sleep(duration)
    return f"Item-{item_id} processed in {duration:.2f}s"

async def main():
    items = list(range(10))
    results = []

    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        # Create tasks dynamically
        tasks = []
        for item_id in items:
            task = tg.create_task(process_item(item_id))
            tasks.append(task)

    # All tasks done, collect results
    for task in tasks:
        results.append(task.result())

    print("Results:")
    for r in results:
        print(f"  {r}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

diagrams.title: TaskGroup: structured concurrency
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  tg["async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg"] --> t1["tg.create_task(a())"]
  tg --> t2["tg.create_task(b())"]
  tg --> t3["tg.create_task(c())"]
  t2 -->|raises| fail["b() fails"]
  fail --> cancel["the group cancels a() and c()"]
  cancel --> exitg["the with-block exits only after every task has finished"]
  exitg --> eg["ExceptionGroup is raised — handle with except*"]
diagrams.explain: A TaskGroup (Python 3.11+) guarantees that no task outlives the block that created it. If one task fails, the siblings are cancelled and the errors are bundled into an `ExceptionGroup`. Prefer it over bare `create_task` + `gather` — it prevents leaked tasks and lost exceptions.

sections.title: 9.3 Cancellation Handling
sections.body:
### Visual Explanation

```
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    CANCELLATION FLOW                                        ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                             ║
║  task.cancel() is called:                                                   ║
║                                                                             ║
║  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  │     task.cancel()                                                    │   ║
║  │          │                                                           │   ║
║  │          ▼                                                           │   ║
║  │    ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │   ║
║  │    │                    TASK                                    │    │   ║
║  │    │                                                            │    │   ║
║  │    │   async def my_task():                                    │    │   ║
║  │    │       try:                                                 │    │   ║
║  │    │           await something()  ◄─── CancelledError raised   │    │   ║
║  │    │       except asyncio.CancelledError:                      │    │   ║
║  │    │           # Cleanup code                                   │    │   ║
║  │    │           raise  # MUST re-raise!                         │    │   ║
║  │    │                                                            │    │   ║
║  │    └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  │    If CancelledError is not re-raised, cancellation is suppressed!  │   ║
║  │                                                                      │   ║
║  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   ║
║                                                                             ║
║  IMPORTANT: Always re-raise CancelledError after cleanup!                   ║
║                                                                             ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

### Code Examples

#### Example 1: Proper Cancellation Handling

```python
import asyncio

async def cleanup_on_cancel():
    """Task that cleans up when cancelled"""
    resource = "allocated_resource"

    try:
        print("Task started, resource allocated")
        await asyncio.sleep(10)
        print("Task completed normally")
        return "success"

    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print("Task was cancelled!")
        print(f"Cleaning up: releasing {resource}")
        # Cleanup code here
        raise  # Always re-raise!

    finally:
        print("Finally block executed")

async def main():
    task = asyncio.create_task(cleanup_on_cancel())

    # Let it run for a bit
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

    # Cancel it
    print("\nRequesting cancellation...")
    task.cancel()

    try:
        await task
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print("Confirmed: task was cancelled")

    print(f"Task cancelled: {task.cancelled()}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 2: Shielding from Cancellation

```python
import asyncio

async def critical_operation():
    """Operation that should complete even if parent is cancelled"""
    print("Critical operation started...")
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    print("Critical operation completed!")
    return "critical_result"

async def cancellable_task():
    """Task with a critical section"""
    print("Starting task...")

    # This part can be cancelled
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

    # This part is shielded from cancellation
    print("Entering critical section...")
    try:
        result = await asyncio.shield(critical_operation())
        print(f"Got result: {result}")
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print("Cancel received, but critical op continues...")
        # The shielded operation continues in background
        raise

    print("Task completed")
    return result

async def main():
    task = asyncio.create_task(cancellable_task())

    # Wait then cancel
    await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
    task.cancel()

    try:
        await task
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print("\nTask was cancelled")

    # Give shielded operation time to complete
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    print("Done waiting for shielded operation")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

#### Example 3: Timeout vs Cancellation

```python
import asyncio

async def long_operation():
    """Long running operation"""
    try:
        print("Long operation started...")
        await asyncio.sleep(10)
        return "completed"
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print("Long operation was cancelled!")
        raise

async def main():
    # Using wait_for with timeout
    print("=== Using wait_for ===")
    try:
        result = await asyncio.wait_for(long_operation(), timeout=2.0)
        print(f"Result: {result}")
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        print("Timed out! (Task was cancelled)")

    # Using timeout context manager (Python 3.11+)
    print("\n=== Using timeout context ===")
    try:
        async with asyncio.timeout(2.0):
            result = await long_operation()
            print(f"Result: {result}")
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        print("Timed out!")

    # Deadline-based timeout (Python 3.11+)
    print("\n=== Using timeout_at ===")
    deadline = asyncio.get_event_loop().time() + 2.0
    try:
        async with asyncio.timeout_at(deadline):
            result = await long_operation()
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        print("Deadline exceeded!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

diagrams.title: How cancellation travels into a task
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Caller
  participant T as Task
  Caller->>T: task.cancel()
  Note over T: CancelledError is raised at the current await
  T->>T: except / finally: release resources
  T-->>Caller: re-raise CancelledError
  Caller->>T: await task raises CancelledError — task.cancelled() is True
diagrams.explain: Cancellation is a **request**: it raises `CancelledError` inside the task at its next await. Clean up in `finally` and let the error propagate — swallowing it breaks `wait_for`, timeouts and TaskGroups. Use `asyncio.shield()` only for short sections that must complete.

sections.title: 9.4 Advanced Task Patterns
sections.body:
### Pattern 1: Task Factory

```python
import asyncio
from typing import Callable, Any

class TaskFactory:
    """Factory for creating and tracking tasks"""

    def __init__(self, name_prefix="Task"):
        self.name_prefix = name_prefix
        self.counter = 0
        self.tasks = {}

    def create(self, coro, on_complete=None):
        """Create and track a task"""
        self.counter += 1
        name = f"{self.name_prefix}-{self.counter}"

        task = asyncio.create_task(coro, name=name)
        self.tasks[name] = task

        def cleanup(t):
            del self.tasks[name]
            if on_complete:
                on_complete(t)

        task.add_done_callback(cleanup)
        return task

    async def wait_all(self):
        """Wait for all active tasks"""
        if self.tasks:
            await asyncio.gather(*self.tasks.values(), return_exceptions=True)

    def cancel_all(self):
        """Cancel all active tasks"""
        for task in self.tasks.values():
            task.cancel()

async def worker(n):
    await asyncio.sleep(n * 0.5)
    return n * 2

async def main():
    factory = TaskFactory("Worker")

    # Create tasks
    for i in range(5):
        factory.create(worker(i))

    print(f"Created {len(factory.tasks)} tasks")

    # Wait for all
    await factory.wait_all()

    print("All tasks completed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Pattern 2: Parallel Map with Limit

```python
import asyncio
from typing import Callable, Iterable, Any

async def parallel_map(
    func: Callable,
    items: Iterable[Any],
    limit: int = 10
) -> list:
    """Map function over items with concurrency limit"""
    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(limit)

    async def limited_func(item):
        async with semaphore:
            return await func(item)

    tasks = [limited_func(item) for item in items]
    return await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

async def process(x):
    print(f"Processing {x}...")
    await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
    return x * 2

async def main():
    items = list(range(20))

    # Process with max 5 concurrent
    results = await parallel_map(process, items, limit=5)

    print(f"\nResults: {results}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Pattern 3: Retry with Backoff

```python
import asyncio
import random

async def retry_async(
    coro_func,
    *args,
    max_retries=3,
    base_delay=1.0,
    backoff_factor=2.0,
    **kwargs
):
    """Retry an async function with exponential backoff"""
    last_exception = None
    delay = base_delay

    for attempt in range(max_retries + 1):
        try:
            return await coro_func(*args, **kwargs)
        except Exception as e:
            last_exception = e
            if attempt < max_retries:
                print(f"Attempt {attempt + 1} failed: {e}. Retrying in {delay}s...")
                await asyncio.sleep(delay)
                delay *= backoff_factor
            else:
                print(f"All {max_retries + 1} attempts failed")

    raise last_exception

async def unreliable_fetch(url):
    """Simulate unreliable network request"""
    if random.random() < 0.7:  # 70% failure rate
        raise ConnectionError(f"Failed to connect to {url}")
    return f"Data from {url}"

async def main():
    try:
        result = await retry_async(
            unreliable_fetch,
            "http://example.com",
            max_retries=5,
            base_delay=0.5
        )
        print(f"Success: {result}")
    except ConnectionError as e:
        print(f"Failed after all retries: {e}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

diagrams.title: Timeouts with asyncio.timeout / wait_for
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  call["async with asyncio.timeout(2)"] --> work["await slow_call()"]
  work -->|"finishes in time"| ok["result"]
  work -->|"deadline passes"| cx["inner task is cancelled"] --> te["TimeoutError raised to the caller"]
diagrams.explain: A timeout is implemented by cancelling the inner work when the deadline passes and converting the resulting `CancelledError` into `TimeoutError`. Put timeouts on every network call: one hung dependency can otherwise hold resources forever.

sections.title: 9.5 Task Scheduling Patterns
sections.body:
### Pattern 1: Periodic Task

```python
import asyncio

async def run_periodically(coro_func, interval, *args, **kwargs):
    """Run a coroutine periodically"""
    while True:
        try:
            await coro_func(*args, **kwargs)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            print("Periodic task cancelled")
            raise
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Periodic task error: {e}")

        await asyncio.sleep(interval)

async def heartbeat():
    """Heartbeat function"""
    print(f"💓 Heartbeat")

async def main():
    # Start periodic task
    task = asyncio.create_task(
        run_periodically(heartbeat, 1.0)
    )

    # Let it run for 5 seconds
    await asyncio.sleep(5)

    # Cancel
    task.cancel()
    try:
        await task
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass

    print("Done!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Pattern 2: Delayed Task

```python
import asyncio

async def run_after(delay, coro):
    """Run a coroutine after a delay"""
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    return await coro

async def scheduled_task(message):
    print(f"Executing: {message}")
    return message

async def main():
    # Schedule tasks at different times
    tasks = [
        asyncio.create_task(run_after(3, scheduled_task("Third"))),
        asyncio.create_task(run_after(1, scheduled_task("First"))),
        asyncio.create_task(run_after(2, scheduled_task("Second"))),
    ]

    # Wait for all
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

### Pattern 3: Priority Queue

```python
import asyncio
import heapq
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

@dataclass(order=True)
class PrioritizedTask:
    priority: int
    task: Any = field(compare=False)

class PriorityTaskQueue:
    def __init__(self, max_concurrent=3):
        self.queue = []
        self.semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)
        self.counter = 0

    def add_task(self, coro, priority=0):
        """Add task with priority (lower = higher priority)"""
        task_wrapper = asyncio.create_task(self._run_task(coro))
        heapq.heappush(self.queue, PrioritizedTask(priority, task_wrapper))
        self.counter += 1

    async def _run_task(self, coro):
        async with self.semaphore:
            return await coro

    async def wait_all(self):
        """Wait for all tasks"""
        tasks = [pt.task for pt in self.queue]
        return await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)

async def task(name, duration):
    print(f"[{name}] Starting")
    await asyncio.sleep(duration)
    print(f"[{name}] Done")
    return name

async def main():
    pq = PriorityTaskQueue(max_concurrent=2)

    # Add tasks with priorities
    pq.add_task(task("Low-1", 1), priority=10)
    pq.add_task(task("High-1", 1), priority=1)
    pq.add_task(task("Medium-1", 1), priority=5)
    pq.add_task(task("High-2", 1), priority=1)

    await pq.wait_all()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

sections.title: Pitfalls & Gotchas
sections.body:
### Orphan Tasks

```python
import asyncio

async def background_task():
    while True:
        print("Background running...")
        await asyncio.sleep(1)

async def bad_practice():
    """Creates orphan task that may not complete"""
    asyncio.create_task(background_task())  # ❌ Never awaited!
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    # Function ends, but background_task keeps running (or is GC'd)

async def good_practice():
    """Properly manage background tasks"""
    task = asyncio.create_task(background_task())
    try:
        await asyncio.sleep(2)
    finally:
        task.cancel()
        try:
            await task
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass
```

### Catching CancelledError Wrong

```python
async def wrong_cancel_handling():
    try:
        await asyncio.sleep(10)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print("Cancelled!")
        # ❌ NOT re-raising - cancellation is suppressed!

async def correct_cancel_handling():
    try:
        await asyncio.sleep(10)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print("Cancelled! Cleaning up...")
        raise  # ✅ Always re-raise!
```
